Plot impulse responses and variance decompositions

Source: R/plot.R
autoplot.varm_irf.Rd

Grid of panels (rows: responding variable, columns: shock) with the point or median response and nested ribbons for each stored level, widest lightest. plot() prints the same ggplot and returns it invisibly.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'varm_irf'
autoplot(
  object,
  shocks = NULL,
  responses = NULL,
  ci = c("band", "line", "none"),
  compare = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'varm_fevd'
autoplot(
  object,
  shocks = NULL,
  responses = NULL,
  ci = c("band", "line", "none"),
  compare = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'varm_dyn'
plot(x, ...)

Arguments

object, x

a varm_irf or varm_fevd object.

shocks, responses

<tidy-select> subsets of the shocks and responding variables, e.g. shocks = rate.

ci

"band" (shaded ribbons, default), "line" (dashed bounds) or "none".

compare

named list of further varm_irf / varm_fevd objects to overlay on object (labelled "Baseline" and the list names), one colour each.

...

unused.

Value

A ggplot object.

See also

Other plotting: autoplot.varm_draws(), autoplot.varm_forecast(), autoplot.varm_hd(), theme_varm()

Examples

fit <- varm(yraw, p = 2)
r <- irf(fit, horizon = 8, ci = "mc", nboot = 100)
ggplot2::autoplot(r)

ggplot2::autoplot(r, shocks = rate, responses = c(infl, unemp))

ggplot2::autoplot(r, ci = "line")

r2 <- irf(varm(yraw, p = 4), horizon = 8, ci = "none")
ggplot2::autoplot(r, compare = list("p = 4" = r2), ci = "none")

ggplot2::autoplot(fevd(fit, horizon = 8, ci = "none"))
